title: fix(driver-sqlite-wasm)!: a file wasm SQLite cannot read is refused at connect, naming the file, instead of being renamed and replaced with an empty database
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wgS2d2sPzGdbRqTa2fsR14Ze)_

Fixes #25019

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none

**Narrowing face:** a connect that resolved over a file wasm SQLite cannot read now rejects, naming the file. `WasmSqliteConnection.open()` no longer renames such a file to `FILE.corrupt-TIMESTAMP` and starts an empty database in its place; `resolveSqliteDriver` re-throws the refusal at the wasm rung instead of trying the in-memory driver. Nothing exported changes shape. It owes a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review before the queue (the claim's line).

Member 3 of the SQLite file-failure family (the wasm quarantine), the card's last member, under the `domain:engine` seat 2's ruling 6311031589 (route A, inherited from #24960's route A). Members 1 and 2 landed in PR #25080 (`d6a5fa3ba`, `Part of #25019`). Dev session `session_015pbbff7SHh7EEEWiasBdDe` (a project card thread of seat session `session_01FaVyM6YvQLg9CsjPVCYc5K`), claim 6335885549; the cross-lane line in `service-datasource` is declared on #21118 (6335909713).

## What changed

- `packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/wasm-connection.ts`
  - `open()`: a file whose bytes sql.js cannot open or read (`new SQL.Database(bytes)` or `PRAGMA quick_check(1)` throws, or `quick_check` does not answer `ok`) is refused with `unreadableDatabaseFileRefusal`: an `Error` carrying `code` (`SQLITE_NOTADB` when SQLite says "file is not a database", `SQLITE_CORRUPT` for every other read failure), `filename`, `cause` (sql.js's own throw), and a message that says how to move the file aside. sql.js throws a bare `Error` with SQLite's message and no result code, so the producer maps SQLite's own errstr for `SQLITE_NOTADB`; nothing downstream reads message text.
  - `quarantineCorruptFile` retires (it was private). The refused file is left byte-for-byte as found and nothing is written beside it.
  - `quarantineOrphanedWal` now runs only after the image is accepted, so a stale write-ahead log beside a refused file stays where it is too.
- `packages/services/service-datasource/src/sqlite-driver-fallback.ts` (the one cross-lane file): the wasm rung's `catch` re-throws when `isSqliteFileOpenFailure(err)` holds, exactly as the native rung does. The predicate needed no new code: the wasm refusal reaches it as `SqlDriver`'s own `SqliteDatabaseFileError` with `SQLITE_NOTADB` / `SQLITE_CORRUPT` (below). Every other wasm failure, sql.js itself not loading first among them, still steps down to the in-memory driver. Module note and predicate doc updated.
- `packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/sqlite-wasm-driver-durability.test.ts`: the self-heal case is now a refusal pin (ruling item 3).
- Pins: `packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/sqlite-wasm-25019-unreadable-file-refused.test.ts` (relative `src` import) and `packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/sqlite-driver-fallback-wasm-unreadable-file.test.ts` (resolves `@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm` through `dist/`).
- Changeset `.changeset/25019-wasm-unreadable-file-refused.md`: `@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm` and `@objectstack/service-datasource` `patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, BREAKING banner (FROM, TO, Unchanged, fix) and ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.

## One vocabulary with the native driver, measured

`SqliteWasmDriver` is a `SqlDriver`, and wasm SQLite's connection is opened by knex's pool on the first statement `SqlDriver.connect()` runs (`PRAGMA auto_vacuum`). The pool propagates the create error (`propagateCreateError: true`), so `applyAutoVacuumIncremental` sees the refusal's `code` and answers it through the same private `SQLITE_FILE_REFUSALS` table the native driver uses, wrapping it in `SqliteDatabaseFileError`. So a wasm refusal carries the native driver's class, code and words ("is not a SQLite database, and was left as it is" / "is damaged (SQLite cannot read its header or its schema), and was left as it is"), with no second phrase table and no edit to `driver-sql`. The prescription is wasm's own cause text, since the rename it replaces was wasm's: the native refusal carries none (the dispatch's assumption that the native family has a move-aside prescription to import did not hold; measured by `grep`, zero hits in `driver-sql/src`).

The line an operator sees (public door below):

```text
datasource 'archive': connect failed — SQLite database file './data/archive.db' (resolved: '…/door/data/archive.db') is not a SQLite database, and was left as it is: wasm SQLite cannot read it (file is not a database). To start from an empty database, move the file aside yourself (mv './data/archive.db' './data/archive.db.unreadable') and start again; to keep its data, restore a copy that opens.
```

## Premise (base `f7d740376`)

`quarantineCorruptFile` was at `wasm-connection.ts`, called from `open()` on a read failure, renaming to `FILE.corrupt-` plus `Date.now()`; the wasm rung of `resolveSqliteDriver` was a bare `catch` stepping down to memory. Both doors were measured by the dev report 6310958104 (open question 1): (a) a declared `sqlite` datasource whose native addon cannot load, over a plain-text or header-truncated file, renamed on a development boot; (b) a datasource declared `driver: 'sqlite-wasm'` over a plain-text file, renamed and `available` in development and production. sql.js 1.14 answers, measured: plain text and magic-header junk throw "file is not a database" at `quick_check`; a real database truncated to 50 bytes or to half throws "database disk image is malformed"; a real database and an empty file answer `ok`.

## Tests

- New pins: `driver-sqlite-wasm` 11/11 across the two files; `service-datasource` 10/10: (a) the native-addon-cannot-load step-down (a real `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` at the #24950 suite's seam) over a plain-text and a header-truncated file rejects with the driver's refusal, no wasm or memory warning, file bytes unchanged, directory holds the file alone; the same through `DatasourceConnectionService` in development reads `failed`, no driver registered; (b) `driver: 'sqlite-wasm'` over both files in development and production reads `failed` with the code's words naming the file, not `available`, nothing moved; (c) controls: a real database opens and answers (wasm, and `sqlite-wasm` declared, both modes `available`), an absent file is created, an empty file opens, a native addon that cannot load over an absent file still steps down to wasm.
- Whole packages (pre-merge head `73dc5b1a`, under the verify lock): `driver-sqlite-wasm` "Test Files 39 passed (39) · Tests 703 passed (703)"; `service-datasource` "Test Files 55 passed (55) · Tests 955 passed (955)"; `typecheck` for both, exit 0.
- Ablation (committed fix at `f8ffdfc0`, `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`): the refusal's `throw` replaced by the old quarantine (rename to `.corrupt-`, empty database, plus a marker), blob `07f7cb3e0fa3` to `15743567f704`; rebuilt; `ablation-dist-preflight` marker present in 2 built files. Predicted and observed: `driver-sqlite-wasm` "6 failed | 5 passed" (the 5 refusal pins and the durability refusal case red; 3 controls and 2 durability cases green); `service-datasource` "7 failed | 3 passed" (all of (a) and (b) red, the 3 controls green). Restore: blob back to `07f7cb3e0fa3` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, rebuilt, preflight `--absent` in 0 of 6 built files, tree clean; both pins green again (11/11, 10/10).

## Public door, measured

`bin/run-dev.js migrate apply --yes` (tsx, built closure), a project declaring `archive` with `driver: 'sqlite-wasm'`, `config.filename: './data/archive.db'`, one object bound, over a 25-byte plain-text file:

- exit 1; the line above, from `✗ Plugin plugin.app.door_25019 failed to start`; md5 `bcbdbe7ff2cba060ed588d3fca48b30c` before and after; `data/` holds `archive.db` alone.
- Following the prescription (`mv './data/archive.db' './data/archive.db.unreadable'`) and running the same command again: exit 0, `datasource 'archive': connected (driver=sqlite-wasm, schemaMode=managed)`, the moved file's md5 unchanged.

## Gates and battery

- Derived set: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `e39b18e5` derived 68; each run once with its exit captured to a file before any pipe. 65 exit 0 on the first pass. Three did not:
  - `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` exit 3: this shallow clone lacked its pinned fixture commit; fetched it, re-run exit 0 (48 cases).
  - `pnpm check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` exit 1: its `objlit` pattern matched the refusal's code TYPE (`code: 'SQLITE_NOTADB' | 'SQLITE_CORRUPT'` in a type literal). The gate's own self-test declares a type annotation is not a stamp and passes a named type, so the type was named (`UnreadableDatabaseFileCode`, `cda55e654`); re-run exit 0 ("56 unregistered code-stamping site(s), all classified"). Disclosed below.
  - `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (eight packages outside this closure have no `dist/`): NOT MEASURED locally, CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` runs it.
- `--ran` at `cda55e654`: "67 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED".
- `check:driver-conformance` before (`f7d740376`) and after: "55 covered cell(s), 0 in the DEBT ledger, 0 exempt" both; dialect axis unchanged.
- `check-platform-checklist` not owed (no exported symbol renamed or removed; `quarantineCorruptFile` was private). `test:repo` and the CLI integration layer not run locally (no such file touched); CI owns them.
- Full dogfood battery at `e39b18e5` (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, the `@objectstack/dogfood^...` closure build, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test`, no shard, no path): lock VERDICT command-exit 1, "Test Files 1 failed | 286 passed | 3 skipped (290) · Tests 2395 passed | 21 skipped (2416)". The one failure is a suite-level `beforeAll` timeout (10 s, `bootShowcase()`) in `test/showcase-single-platform-insert-default-organization.dogfood.test.ts`, before any of its 3 tests. Re-run alone it times out the same way, and the CONTROL (the same file with `wasm-connection.ts` restored to base `f7d740376` and rebuilt, `quarantineCorruptFile` present in `dist/`) times out identically, so it is not this change: the showcase boots a fresh wasm database (no file to refuse) and runs out of hook time on this shared box. Tree restored and rebuilt after the control (`dist/index.mjs` md5 back to `11790b18…`). CI's full battery is the reading of record.
- The only commit after the battery is `cda55e654` (a type alias): rebuilt `dist/index.mjs` and `dist/index.js` are byte-identical before and after it (md5 `11790b18…`, `f3177051…`).

## Acceptance notes

- **Level `patch`, not the ruling's `minor`.** The ruling's item 4 names `minor`; the level now follows the metadata-protocol kind alone (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, maintainer ruling A on #25105), and nothing a metadata author writes changes here, so the kind is `none`, which the gate grades `patch` and refuses at `minor`. BREAKING-ness is carried by the `Clause-②` arm, the banner and the ADR-0087 disposition, as `24837-managed-datasource-sync-refused.md` does. The seat may re-grade.
- **The ruling's named cost:** a development server whose own wasm image is damaged no longer starts itself clean; the refusal's prescription says how to move the file aside, and the public door above shows that step working.
- knex logs `Acquire connection error:` with the refusal's stack at `warn` once per acquire attempt (its own logger, `knex/lib/client.js`). The native refusal never fails an acquire, so it does not print this; every other dialect's acquire failure (a refused PG connection) does. Noted, not filed.
- Named only, per family note 6305864303: the development telemetry sibling (`packages/cli/src/utils/telemetry-datasource.ts`) still catches every throw, so a damaged telemetry sibling is now neither renamed nor reported. Pre-existing best-effort shape, out of the claim.
- #25084 (the refused-connect handle) is not addressed here; a wasm refusal holds no connection (the open failed before the pool kept one).
- `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`: the refusal stamps SQLite's own result-code names (`SQLITE_NOTADB` / `SQLITE_CORRUPT`) through a ternary assignment, a position outside that gate's declared population, as `driver-sql` carries the same names (copied from better-sqlite3's error, and as `SQLITE_FILE_REFUSALS` keys). They are foreign vocabulary, not ADR-0112 codes. A `foreign-vocabulary` row in `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts` would make that explicit; it is outside this claim's file surface, so it is left to the seat.
- Every read failure other than SQLite's "file is not a database" is classified `SQLITE_CORRUPT`: the bytes were read off disk and sql.js could not read them as a database, which is the file's verdict. An operating-system failure reading the file (`EACCES`) is not this path and is unchanged.
